subject: Geo-differentiated capacity ask: US/EU/APAC SKU allocation and latency targets
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walker <sam.walker@helix.ai>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@nova-ml.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Geo-differentiated capacity ask: US/EU/APAC SKU allocation and latency targets

Hi Sam / Priya —

Following our discovery last week, Helix confirmed expected Q3+ usage growth across three regions. We put together an initial ask to size dedicated capacity by geography so we can draft a committed SKU proposal and estimate latency SLO impacts. High-level goal: keep 95th percentile gen latency under 350ms for US and EU; APAC target 420ms with burst buffer for launch week.

Attached: geo-demand-matrix.xlsx (workload forecasts by model/route) and a first-pass SKU mapping. Can you confirm the following by EOD Tuesday?
- Expected 95th pctl traffic split (US / EU / APAC) for steady-state and peak week
- Whether EU needs data residency-only (no on-prem) or a private deployment option
- Any hard SLA or audit requirements we should factor into dedicated sizing

Karthik / Ben: could you review the attached matrix and comment on the mapping assumptions (GPU types, burst lanes, sustained RPS per slot)? I paired nominal model profiles with peak token rates in the sheet.

Thanks — I can book a quick 30-min sync after we get the numbers.

— Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
+1 (408) 555-0142

Attachments: geo-demand-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed-sku-mapping.pdf (pdf)

From: Sam Walker <sam.walker@helix.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geo-differentiated capacity ask: US/EU/APAC SKU allocation and latency targets

Thanks Jasmine — quick answers inline.

• Traffic split (steady / peak week): US 58% / 52%, EU 28% / 30%, APAC 14% / 18%. Peak week assumes new feature launch with routed inference for 30% of calls.
• EU residency: yes — must be EU-only control plane and data at rest in EU region for that product line.
• SLA needs: 99.5% uptime; audit readiness for SOC-type logs but we can start with standard evidence packets and escalate if required.

We reviewed the matrix with our infra team — two asks: add a small burst lane capacity for APAC launch day (simulated 4x baseline for 6 hours) and show cost delta for GPU A100 -> H100 mixes in EU. Happy to join a sync after Karthik's sizing notes.

— Sam Walker
Head of Platform, Helix AI
sam.walker@helix.ai
+44 20 7946 0958

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Walker <sam.walker@helix.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geo-differentiated capacity ask: US/EU/APAC SKU allocation and latency targets

Jasmine / team — reviewed the demand matrix. A few technical clarifications and recommended sizing items: 

1) Baseline instance types: map steady-state to H100-80GB fractional quantized (for cost/QPS balance); EU residency lanes should use dedicated H100s to avoid cross-tenant noisy-neighbor risk.
2) APAC burst: propose two short-lived burst pools (edge-burst-1 and edge-burst-2) consuming reserved credits and a soft autoscale cap at 6x baseline. We'll model warm KV cache priming cost.
3) Latency targets: 95th <350ms (US/EU) is achievable if we reserve +20% headroom on GPU counts for 95th pctl and enable continuous batching thresholds tuned per route. For APAC 420ms, need local GPU presence or a high-performance edge POP paired with a fallback region; otherwise networking will dominate.
4) Cost sensitivity: I'll run three scenarios (H100-only, H100+A100 mixed, A100-only) and export a cost per-100k tokens delta for each region. Expect to have the scenario PDFs by tomorrow afternoon.

Action items: Ben to validate RPS->GPU slot conversions; Jasmine to confirm Helix's EU residency constraints for private control plane.

— Karthik Iyer
Senior Infrastructure Systems Eng, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Walker <sam.walker@helix.ai>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@nova-ml.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geo-differentiated capacity ask: US/EU/APAC SKU allocation and latency targets

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Sam. Next steps and timeline: 

- Karthik will share three cost/latency scenarios by Tue 18 Mar EOD (H100-only / mixed / A100-only).
- Ben and Connor will translate steady-state + peak splits into SKU counts and draft a reserved commitment schedule; expect a first-pass SOW-friendly SKU table by Wed morning.
- Sam / Priya: confirm whether Helix wants the EU lane as Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) or Dedicated with EU-only tenancy. That decision impacts pricing and lead time.

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up Wed 18 Mar 10:00 AM PT to walk through scenarios unless you propose an alternate. If you need the burst-run numbers sooner for launch planning, flag and we can accelerate.

Thanks — attaching the updated demand matrix with a small note column where I captured Sam's burst ask.

— Jasmine
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: geo-demand-matrix.xlsx (updated), proposed-sku-mapping.pdf (v2)
